p.i: Per saxa, & ignes sollicitum rapit: Quem non morantur saeva bruma Frigora, nec maris inquieti Fluctus, vt addat gaudia gaudijs, Vtque auctioris summa pecunia Accrescat, vt votis potitus Vitam agat vsque beatiorem: Quem non fatigant pondera grandia: Qui pertinaci diffugientia Mercatur inuisa quietis Commoda, non sapiens, labore: Vt plena tandem diuitijs domus Amplis nitescat: quid facere hunc putas? Insanus, in se tollit ipsum Tecta grani ruitura lapsu.

main_text.head: XXI. GAL.
main_text.p: A RRESTE: Atten:ô Mondain, où cours-tu? Escoute, entens la voix de la Vertu. Las! il passe outre : il court apres le Monde, Et va courant, fuyant, ainsi que l'onde D'vn gros torrent, que l'orage des cieux Fondu en bas a rendu orgueilleux. Ma remonstrance, est vn roc, qu'il rencontre Passant dessus, murmurant à l'encontre.

page.notes: Top verse block is set in italic and is Latin; the first word "Per" has a large initial P. The heading "XXI. GAL." is set in small capitals. The French stanza's initial A is a large woodcut-style initial, transcribed as "A RRESTE" (the A joined to RRESTE). "H 4" at the foot is a signature mark and is recorded in the main text above as a gathering mark; it may belong in <signature> instead. Some letters in the French lines are faint: "Atten:ô" and "fuyant" are read with reasonable confidence; "orgueilleux" and "murmurant" are clear. The Latin line "Quem non morantur saeva bruma" is slightly uncertain in "bruma" (printed "brumæ" with a ligature). The line "Frigora, nec maris inquieti" has a faint "inquieti". No running-head number present beyond 119.
